name: Hardware Additions

attack_mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network

evidence.rationale: Adversaries may introduce unauthorized devices onto the network. ATT&CK recommends network access controls such as 802.1X, device certificates, and restricting DHCP to registered devices; these are architectural admission-control mechanisms that directly prevent unauthorized hardware from communicating with trusted systems.

Adversaries can attach rogue computers, appliances, or networking hardware to obtain enterprise network connectivity. Secure network management protocols like 802.1X requires successful user or device authentication before network admission, directly denying unauthorized hardware access.

Port-level access control using 802.1X, device certificates, or similar network access control mechanisms can prevent unauthorized hardware from authenticating to and communicating on trusted enterprise networks.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
'none' or 'no_row' means the mapping has no mitigating control. It does not mean that no defence exists.
Claims use ATT&CK Enterprise 16.1, the version that the source mapping uses. See later_version for changes in newer versions.
CIS claims (cis_claims and cis/safeguards) use ATT&CK Enterprise 19.1, the version that the CIS mapping uses.
